written_by: breach owner, BEFORE the re-bake finished and BEFORE any frame was re-rendered
written_at: 2026-08-03, while the 1,657-frame bake at bond 100 / mullion 40/120 was at frame ~1 of 1657
what_this_is: A prediction, recorded so it can be wrong. Nothing in this file was read off the new bake. The only numbers here that come from a bake are the SHIPPED 4000 figures I am predicting AGAINST, which are the previous agent's and are quoted as the null hypothesis.

THE_ARTEFACT_BEING_PREDICTED.seen: render/breach_f9/f9_1920_f0866.png. The east wall reads as a soup of hard-edged translucent slabs, several deep, at multiple orientations, spanning the whole glazing. I have looked at it; it is real and it is gross.
THE_ARTEFACT_BEING_PREDICTED.the_falsified_hypothesis: that the intact pane and its shards both render for ~12 frames. apply_breach.py hides the pane and shows the shards at the SAME frame r = min(release) per bay, and no frame renders both. The only real doubling is 9 shards in bays 5 and 7 that appear at 861, which is a ONE-frame 9-shard HOLE, not a 12-frame whole-wall double.
THE_ARTEFACT_BEING_PREDICTED.the_surviving_explanation: the shard field itself. At t_bond_per_m 4000 the glass does not leave: bay 4's panes bulge outboard AS A COHERENT SHEET and then spring back. Bay 4's median depth offset is 483 mm at f866 and 17 mm by f900. ~3,000 flat plates spread through ~1.4 m of depth, seen through one another, and then RE-ASSEMBLING. The take therefore contains a shatter-and-un-shatter: the wall un-breaks on camera, in a film with no cuts.
THE_ARTEFACT_BEING_PREDICTED.frame_facts: impact is film frame 859.88; RELEASE_FRAME = 860; every fractured bay's pane hides and its shards appear at 860. So f0855-f0859 is intact pane, f0860 onward is shards.

THE_MECHANISM_I_AM_BETTING_ON: at 4000 the bond network is 40x stronger than the glass it represents, so the impact cannot part the sheet: it loads it, the sheet stores the energy elastically across 12,756 inter-shard constraints, and the constraint network gives it back. That is a trampoline, not a fracture. At 100 the bonds part where they are loaded, each shard's momentum becomes its own, and there is nothing left to pull it home. A field that has separated has no restoring force.

P1_no_spring_back.claim: bay 4's median depth offset |x - x0| is MONOTONICALLY NON-DECREASING from f860 to f900, to within noise, and at f900 it is at least 5x its f866 value.
P1_no_spring_back.null_it_is_against: the shipped 4000: 483 mm at f866 falling to 17 mm at f900 - a 28x COLLAPSE.
P1_no_spring_back.falsified_if: the f900 median is below the f866 median at all. Any net return of the field is the shatter-and-un-shatter surviving the fix, and that is a second defect.
P1_no_spring_back.instrument: sim/out/breach_film.npz (the resampled film-frame table) for the new bake, bay 4 shards only, median over shards of |x(f) - x(860)|. Same instrument the 483/17 figures came from.

P2_the_stack_does_not_form.claim: the DEPTH SPREAD of bay 4's shards (p90 minus p10 of x) at f866 will be LARGER than the 4000 bake's 1.4 m, not smaller - the glass is leaving faster - but the field will be SPARSE rather than a stack: the shards will not be co-planar, because they will have parted and rotated.
P2_the_stack_does_not_form.why_this_matters: the slab look is not caused by depth spread alone. It is caused by ~3,000 plates that are still ALIGNED WITH EACH OTHER and with the wall plane, offset in depth. Alignment is what makes a stack of glass read as slabs; a genuinely fractured field reads as a cloud. So the honest picture-side test is angular, not positional.
P2_the_stack_does_not_form.instrument: per-shard quaternion from the bake: the angle between each shard's normal at f866 and its normal at f859. At 4000 a sheet that bulges keeps its normals; at 100 they should scatter.
P2_the_stack_does_not_form.falsified_if: the median normal rotation at f866 is under ~5 deg, i.e. the field is still a sheet.

P3_the_picture.claim: re-rendered f0855-f0890 will show, at f0866, discrete separating fragments with OPEN AIR and the outdoor plaza visible between them across bay 4, and NOT a continuous field of overlapping parallel translucent plates. By f0880-f0890 there will be a visibly growing hole with the car through it.
P3_the_picture.how_I_will_judge_it: by looking at the frames, at 1920 first and then at 3840 on the one that matters, exactly as the artefact was found. Plus the bay rectangles projected through the real camera onto the render, the way sim/tmp/f0866_bays.png was made, so the claim 'inside bay 4' is measured and not eyeballed.
P3_the_picture.falsified_if: the slabs are still there. If they survive the new configuration then the cause is NOT the bond threshold, it is something in apply_breach.py's shard material or its hide keys, and it is a second, separate defect that I want to name.

P4_the_one_frame_hole_survives.claim: the 9-shard one-frame hole at 860/861 is NOT fixed by this change - it comes from release frames that are not all equal within a bay, which is a resample/apply artefact and has nothing to do with thresholds. I predict it is still present after the re-bake and re-apply.
P4_the_one_frame_hole_survives.falsified_if: release_frame_min is 860 and every fractured bay's shards appear at 860 with none at 861.

WHAT_WOULD_MAKE_ME_WRONG_IN_AN_INTERESTI: if the glass leaves cleanly (P1 and P2 hold) but the picture still reads as slabs (P3 fails). That would mean the artefact was never about the wall's motion at all, and the whole shatter-and-un-shatter reading - which is a good reading and explains the 483 -> 17 mm collapse - would still be TRUE and still be a defect, but not THIS defect. I would then look at the shard material's thickness, its IOR, and whether apply_breach is instancing a flat plate rather than the fractured solid.
WHAT_I_CANNOT_PREDICT: whether the field is at rest by the end. Every sweep point so far ended with the field still in flight, and the bake is frozen by CONSTANT extrapolation at its last key with 2,375 bodies still moving over 1 mm/frame. That is off camera, so nothing is SEEN to stop, but it means the aperture I measure at the last frame is a lower bound and the settled aperture is unknown.

ADDENDUM_1_written_before_the_new_bake_l.when: after building sim/slabcheck.py and running it on the SHIPPED 4000 bake, still before the new bake finished and before any frame was re-rendered
ADDENDUM_1_written_before_the_new_bake_l.why_this_is_here: P2's REASONING is falsified by the shipped data, before the new bake has anything to say. I am recording that rather than quietly dropping it.

P2_reasoning_was_wrong.I_claimed: at 4000 a sheet that bulges keeps its normals, so the slab look is an ALIGNMENT effect and the honest test is angular. I set the falsifier at 'median normal rotation under ~5 deg at f866'.
P2_reasoning_was_wrong.the_shipped_bake_says: bay 4's median normal rotation at f866 is 80.7 deg and bay 5's is 89.0 deg. The shards have comprehensively rotated. The field at f866 is NOT a coherent sheet, so the slab look cannot be an alignment-preserving sheet, and my falsifier would have 'passed' the new bake for the wrong reason.
P2_reasoning_was_wrong.what_is_actually_diagnostic: the RETURN, and it is a return in BOTH quantities. Bay 4: depth 483 mm and 80.7 deg at f866, back to 16.7 mm and 9.9 deg at f900. The field rotates out and then rotates BACK. That is the strongest single statement of the defect available: a field that has genuinely fractured cannot un-rotate. Twelve thousand seven hundred and fifty-six bonds that never broke are holding every shard on a rubber band.

P1_stands_and_is_now_quantified_with_a_s.instrument: sim/slabcheck.py, six controls, all firing, referenced to HOME and not to the swap frame

shipped_4000_bay_3.note: bay 3 barely moves at all at 4000, so its 'LEAVES' is not a departure, it is a bay that never went anywhere. The verdict word is about the SHAPE of the curve, not about the size of the hole. Read it with the peak.

P1_stands_and_is_now_quantified_with_a_s.the_prediction_restated_against_this_ins: at bond 100 / mullion 40/120, bays 4 and 5 must come back LEAVES with a peak that keeps rising, and their alignment at the last frame must NOT fall back toward zero. If bay 4 comes back RETURNS the fix has failed on its own terms.

A_MISTAKE_OF_MINE_WORTH_RECORDING.what: slabcheck first referenced depth to the SWAP FRAME rather than to home. It read 361 mm at f866 where the previous agent read 483 mm, and I nearly reported their figure as unreproducible.
A_MISTAKE_OF_MINE_WORTH_RECORDING.the_reason: by the swap frame the glass HAS ALREADY MOVED - a median 128.9 mm and a maximum 350.2 mm for bay 4. One film frame spans the entire impact: frame 859 is 36.5 ms before contact and frame 860 is 5.1 ms after it. The swap frame is not a state of rest and is not a valid zero.
A_MISTAKE_OF_MINE_WORTH_RECORDING.checked_against_the_raw_bake_because_a_r: no. In the 240 Hz world-time bake bay 4 is at 0.00 mm at sim frame 141, 1.66 mm at 144, 35 mm at 145 and 105 mm at 146, advancing at 16.8 m/s - the car's own speed, to three digits. The motion is physical and the resample is faithful to it. There is no pop at the swap beyond what the car does.
A_MISTAKE_OF_MINE_WORTH_RECORDING.so: the previous agent's numbers were right and my instrument was wrong. It now reproduces 483.1 and 16.7 exactly, and it reports `moved_by_the_swap_frame` on every bay so this particular trap is visible in the output rather than in someone's memory.

ADDENDUM_2_P1_TESTED_EARLY_ON_THE_300_FR.result: P1 IS CONFIRMED at the recommended configuration.
ADDENDUM_2_P1_TESTED_EARLY_ON_THE_300_FR.reading: at the shipped 4000, bay 4 ends with ZERO PER CENT of its glass more than 250 mm from home after peaking at 818 mm. That is the un-shatter, stated as plainly as it can be. At the recommended configuration 97.8 % of bay 4 is gone and stays gone. The stack cannot form because there is no stack.
ADDENDUM_2_P1_TESTED_EARLY_ON_THE_300_FR.an_unexpected_one: m1's glass does not fly as FAR as sw_b100's (peak 2,348 mm against 3,963 mm) but far MORE of it leaves (97.8 % against 90.1 %). That is what breaking the mullion does: the frame absorbs energy instead of holding the glass, so the field is slower and larger. It also matches the previous agent's aperture figure (96.8 % vacated) from a completely different instrument, which is the best independent check available that either is right.
ADDENDUM_2_P1_TESTED_EARLY_ON_THE_300_FR.bays_3_and_6_do_not_move_at_any_setting: DID_NOT_MOVE, 0.0 % and 0.5 % gone at the recommended configuration, against a plan that marks them `destroyed`. This is R2-095 seen from a second instrument: the impact reaches bays 4 and 5 and mullion 5 and nothing else.
ADDENDUM_2_P1_TESTED_EARLY_ON_THE_300_FR.P2_and_P3_still_open: P2's ALIGNMENT figure is 107.6 deg at f866, but I have withdrawn P2's reasoning (see addendum 1) so this neither confirms nor refutes anything. P3 is a picture claim and is not settled until frames are rendered and looked at.

ADDENDUM_3_P4_WILL_BE_FALSIFIED_BY_MY_OW.P4_said: the 9-shard one-frame hole at 860/861 comes from release frames that are not all equal within a bay, has nothing to do with thresholds, and will still be present after the re-bake and re-apply.
ADDENDUM_3_P4_WILL_BE_FALSIFIED_BY_MY_OW.the_first_half_is_right: it is a release-spread artefact and no threshold touches it. sim/verify_breach.py --swap reads the table and reports it: 7 shards in bay 5 and 2 in bay 7 at 861 against a pane that hides at 860. And --swap-scene reads the APPLIED SCENE and reports the same 7 and 2, so it is real in the artefact that renders, not only in the table.
ADDENDUM_3_P4_WILL_BE_FALSIFIED_BY_MY_OW.the_second_half_will_be_wrong_because_I_: I fixed the applier. The swap frame is now computed ONCE per bay and both the pane and every one of its shards key off it, so the hole cannot form regardless of what the release column says. Predicting that a defect will persist and then fixing it is not a failed prediction, but it is not a confirmed one either, and it would be dishonest to score it as a hit.
ADDENDUM_3_P4_WILL_BE_FALSIFIED_BY_MY_OW.what_will_actually_be_checked: --swap-scene on the newly applied scene must come back PASS with zero problems. The table arm will still report the spread, deliberately: the spread is the raw material of the defect and the applier is the only thing standing between it and a hole in the picture. An applier can be changed back.

ADDENDUM_4_BY_COUNT_IS_NOT_BY_AREA.how_I_found_it: I looked at sim/out/gone_m1.png, the elevation of the recommended configuration, and bay 5 read as MOSTLY STILL GLAZED while my instrument said 87.1 % of it had gone. I disbelieved the instrument. The instrument was right and the number was the wrong number.
ADDENDUM_4_BY_COUNT_IS_NOT_BY_AREA.the_reason: bay 5's shard sizes are heavily skewed - median 0.00043 m2 against a p90 of 0.018 - and it is the SMALL cells that leave. 87.1 % of bay 5's SHARDS are more than 250 mm from home and only 13.2 % of its AREA is, because the 12.9 % that stayed are the big ones. An aperture is an area.
ADDENDUM_4_BY_COUNT_IS_NOT_BY_AREA.it_reconciles_with_the_previous_agent_ex: their 96.8 % vacated for bay 4 at m1 and 58.2 % at sw_b100 are reproduced to the decimal by a different instrument, and the shipped bake's bay 5 at 3.5 % matches breach_metrics' own per-bay raster figure. Two instruments that were built independently now agree, which is the best evidence available that either is right.
ADDENDUM_4_BY_COUNT_IS_NOT_BY_AREA.and_it_sharpens_the_result: at the recommended configuration bay 4 vacates 96.8 % of its area floor to head and bay 5 vacates 13.2 %. The opening really is ONE BAY plus the mullion the car struck. That is the honest shape of it, and it is why the declared 9.6 m was never going to come out of this impact.
ADDENDUM_4_BY_COUNT_IS_NOT_BY_AREA.slabcheck_now_reports_both: and labels the count figure BY COUNT, because I nearly quoted it as an aperture.
